tells: 1. Back half of the room is flat, untextured black silhouette cut-outs standing in haze; they read as 2D cards pasted behind the lit rows, with no rim light, no parallax cue and no seats (club-1-wide.png and club-6-held.png, upper-middle band behind row 1, y 200-420)

2. The laugh barely happens: across six frames only the white-shirt woman lifts a hand to her mouth and the green-hoodie man turns his head; everyone else holds the same table-hands pose, so nothing reads as caused by a line (club-5-strip.png, all six frames, centre tables)

3. The face close shows a dark outline halo along the jacket collar and shoulder against the defocused background, plus waxy, uniformly lit skin and glassy eyes with no wet highlight; it reads as a 2008 game asset, not a person (club-4-face.png, shoulder and collar edge, x 330-1100, y 380-720; eyes)

4. Many people share the same 'forearms on table, hands clasped by the candle' rest pose, and the held frame is almost identical to mid 2, so the room feels posed and frozen (club-2-mid.png vs club-6-held.png, the tables at x 360-1020)

5. The far-right figures are mangled and murky: one man's legs and torso twist into the shadow with an unreadable silhouette, and stray green and blue specks float in the haze like dead pixels (club-1-wide.png, right edge x 1140-1280, y 380-600; green dots near x 175,265 and x 870,280)

2. The front row repeats one pose, hands on knees and back upright, so it reads as a mannequin line; the second row's torsos stand stiffly in the gaps (theatre-6-held.png and theatre-1-wide.png, front row x 280-1100, y 430-720)

3. The laughing mouth in the close is a flat black hole with no teeth, tongue or inner lip shading, and the hoodie edges carry a dark outline halo against the blurred background (theatre-4-face.png, mouth x 590-700, y 400-470; hoodie edge x 380-1060)

4. Back-of-house silhouettes are flat black cut-outs over a blue haze, and the hard red tint on the left-side spectators' clothes looks like a shader error rather than seat bounce (theatre-2-mid.png top band y 30-220; theatre-3-mid.png left group x 120-220, y 380-480)

5. The laugh does build (mouths open from t=12.6, the cap man leans in, the blonde ducks), but the back two rows and the right-hand block never change, and the beanie man's hair is a low-res smeared texture cap (theatre-5-strip.png, rows 2-3 and right third; theatre-3-mid.png x 1150-1240, y 370-430)

2. The face close's hair has a jagged, aliased dark fringe and a black halo where the hair cards meet the blurred background; the skin is uniform wax with no subsurface (openmic-4-face.png, hair edge x 760-890, y 0-380; ear x 750-820)

3. Most of the room keeps hands on knees and leans forward identically; in the wide, two-thirds of the audience share the same hunched pose, which reads as cloned (openmic-1-wide.png and openmic-6-held.png, front rows x 120-1100)

4. Posture breaks: the dark-hoodie woman's legs go pink and stocking-like and cross into her neighbour; the red-jacket man's forearm sinks into his thigh (openmic-1-wide.png x 710-800, y 590-700; openmic-6-held.png x 940-1020, y 600-700)

5. The reaction is local: only the green-shirt and hoodie women laugh and turn to each other (good, it reads as social), but the four men on the left stay neutral and static through the whole strip, so the room's laugh never spreads (openmic-5-strip.png, left half of every frame)
